risk_summary: BLOCKED by phase_alignment_status (allowed=false, alignment_status=ambiguous_requires_block): Constitutional terminology rename lacks verified semantic equivalence, cascades into snapshot contract phrasing (CLAUDE.md Section 6 uses 'Layer 3+'), and creates a code-doc naming schism with unchanged code paths (layer2/, layer2/index_suite.py).

BLOCKED by role_citation_verdict (overall_status=conflict_requires_block): Multiple RC-4 verdicts — C-001 (Layer 2→truth_store) and C-002 (Layer 3→decision_layer) lack citation to SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_AND_BUILD_SEQUENCE_v1.md; C-004 (README_LAYER2.md rename) would invalidate CLAUDE.md §2.1 canonical document set without constitutional amendment.
BLOCKED by audit_summary (overall_audit_status=blocked, fail_closed_applied=true): Deep audit synthesized 1 blocking violation from phase_alignment_status.

Unverified semantic equivalence: Neither 'truth_store' nor 'decision_layer' appears in any canonical current-state document. Per CLAUDE.md §5.3, asserted equivalence does not count as proof. 'truth_store' may under-represent Layer 2 scope (ingestion, adapters, snapshot publication, registry, snapshot boundary). 'decision_layer' may under-represent Layer 3 scope (Feature Builder, Index Suite, Regime Gate, Supervisor Engine, Decision Engine, DecisionPacket generation).

Constitutional self-modification risk: CLAUDE.md itself uses 'Layer 2' and 'Layer 3' as foundational defined terms in Sections 2, 3, 4, 6, and 11. Modifying these terms changes the language of governance enforcement — a meta-governance change of the highest severity.

README_LAYER2.md filename rename requires constitutional amendment: The filename is explicitly enumerated in CLAUDE.md §2.1 (canonical current-state sources) and §2.2 (canonical role definitions). Renaming without amending CLAUDE.md §2.1 would break the canonical document set definition and all downstream validators that reference it by name.

Code-doc naming schism: Code paths (layer2/, layer2/index_suite.py) retain 'layer2' naming. A documentation-only rename without synchronous code rename creates a persistent naming divergence between implementation and documentation, violating CLAUDE.md §11 code-documentation alignment requirement.

Governance workflow cascade risk: Agent definitions, skill instructions, and system-orchestration.yaml reference Layer 2/3 terminology. Partial rename creates an internally inconsistent governance system. Phase alignment independently confirmed: partial application is blocked; full synchronous cascade is a prerequisite, not a follow-up.

Snapshot contract terminology stability at risk: CLAUDE.md §6.1 states 'Layer 3+ MUST read ONLY from published snapshots.' Renaming must preserve the exact semantics of the downstream consumption rule. The proposed term 'decision_layer+' has not been evaluated for semantic clarity in this context.
notes: This change was blocked at three governance layers (phase alignment, role citation, deep audit). No code or documentation was accepted. The blocked attempt is itself a governance event.

change_mode classified as content_change, not rename_only: semantic equivalence of the replacement terms is unverified (claim c5 evidence_class=cannot_verify_from_current_materials, confidence_level=low). Per DR-11, a purported rename that cannot demonstrate semantic invariance must not be classified as rename_only.

The terminology being renamed is current-state documentation even where it refers to target-state components (Layer 3). The claim_classification_map correctly identifies dominant_scope as current-state.
No target-state work has been described as current-state implementation. Layer 3 components remain 'not yet built' per current canonical docs; this assessment is unaffected by the blocked rename.
Doc-only change does not alter runtime evidence status — but this change was blocked before any documentation was modified.

Per phase_alignment_status recommended_next_step: if the terminology change is still desired, a constitutional amendment process is required involving (1) verified semantic equivalence, (2) single coordinated change across all artifacts, and (3) full doc-code-sync-check and deep audit routing before application.
